QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_43

question.text: Tax-free bonds issued under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, offer:

answer.text: Complete exemption of interest income from tax

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax-free bonds have absolute tax exemption on interest under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act, 1961. The interest received by the bondholder is exempt from income tax. The Trap: Tax-saving bonds, by contrast, offer interest that is taxable; tax-free bonds exempt the interest income itself, not the investment amount. STT and indexation are unrelated benefits. Note: The distinction between tax-free and tax-saving bonds is the key takeaway from the source page.
